column7: Verilog and SystemVerilog decisions decompose into stable independently addressable atomic conditions without changing expression structure
VHDL Boolean decisions use the same stable atomic-condition model while retaining language-specific operators and source identity
Condition outcome recording preserves every governed short-circuit rule and never evaluates an operand the source execution would skip
Atomic conditions record true and false outcomes, and an unknown operand ends the evaluation walk without scoring either binary result
Expression rows are the reachable short-circuit evaluation paths of a decision, and a decision beyond the operand or row bound is skipped rather than partly scored
Each selected binary bit owns separate zero-to-one and one-to-zero bins with stable identity and no transition-direction aliasing
Verilog and SystemVerilog ports nets signals and retained variables receive bounded toggle inventories with exact hierarchical ownership
VHDL entity ports and architecture signals receive equivalent bounded toggle inventories, reading STD_ULOGIC through its X01 projection
Automatic locals are not toggle objects, and memories and arrays of words are excluded from toggle scoring by default with an inspectable reason row
Memories and arrays of words are never silently tracked or partly scored, and each appears once as an excluded row with a stable reason instead of element bins
Transitions to or from unknown or high-impedance values never satisfy either binary toggle bin
Enum and case driven state objects are inferred only from unambiguous governed evidence with stable state identities
Optional next-state objects and declared legal-state sets augment current-state inference without manufacturing missing states or transitions
SystemVerilog fsm_current_state, fsm_next_state and fsm_legal_states module pragmas select and constrain inferred machines
VHDL source hints and language-neutral manifest hints share one validated machine description without changing HDL semantics
FSM state visits and legal transitions keep separate counters, identities and aggregation across instances and engines, with other transitions reported excluded
Invalid pragma, source-attribute and manifest FSM descriptions are rejected with a stable diagnostic instead of being credited
